# Independent whole383 mathematical decision and reconstructed foundation

This is an unverified independent research draft, 9 October 2026. No incoming correctness grant is used. My scoped mathematical decision is positive for the finite base-field Picard bridge, the consequent base-field nonalgebraization, and the ordinary bounded/operator/energy/circle claims, with the published analytic foundations stated below. This decision concerns the arguments, not acceptance, publication, execution, or a fresh reconstruction of every deeper cited foundation. The original P16.7 verdict is false. The entire 66,573-byte companion was read; its five expanded bodies and the 21,055-byte ledger were separately identified as exact substrings. All five DIFFERENT actual final texts and their outside fields were read, with the truncated middle of actual n3 repaired. Their historical reading attestations are data, not mine. Earlier historical proofs and all book chapters are not claimed freshly read in this turn. The supplied TeX is a distinct encoded version; its new theorem statements and preamble were read and its full body encoding is checked separately.

## Retained field and exact finite Picard theorem

Let K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8. Every finite product of closed discs, circles, and closed annuli with positive radii in |K*| has analytic Picard group zero. In particular Pic(P_m)=0 for every integer m>=1, where P_m has |s|^m<=|z_j|<=|s|^(-m), j=1,2. No arbitrary-extension assertion is needed here.

The exact external input is Gruson, *Fibres vectoriels sur un polydisque ultrametrique*, Ann. Sci. ENS (4) 1 (1968), 45--89, IV.5, Theorem 1, printed pp.79--81. For a complete real-valued K, put D=Q tensor v(K*). His disc algebra T_(1,r), r in D, consists of series sum a_i X^i with v(a_i)+ir tending to infinity; C consists of Laurent series with v(a_i) tending to infinity as |i| tends to infinity. If H is a completed tensor product of these disc and circle algebras, H is topologically finite type and filtered-noetherian, satisfies (R), and SK^0(H)=SK^1(H)=0. Here SK^0 is coker(Z->K^0(H)), 1->[H]; (R) is finite homological dimension for the appropriate finitely generated graded modules. Only SK^0 is applied. The full immediate proof passes to gr(H)=gr(K)[X_1,...,X_p,Y_1^+-1,...,Y_q^+-1]. Graded semisimplicity, polynomial graded K-theory and homogeneous localization give stable graded freeness; the filtered lifting results IV.2 give SK^0(H)=0. The separate SK^1/excellence argument is not used. Those deeper K-theory inputs remain the published theorem's dependencies, not newly proved assertions here. The authentic local full text/PDF and the complete LF1510--1690 source unit were checked. No wide annulus is inserted into H.

By coherent-affinoid correspondence a line bundle on a pure disc/circle product is a rank-one finite projective H-module P. SK^0=0 gives [P]=n[H]; rank gives n=1. Equality in the group completion of the direct-sum monoid means P+Q is isomorphic to H+Q for some finite projective Q. Its rank is locally constant; determinants on the rank components give P tensor det Q = det Q, hence P=H. Radii in |K*| are rescaled to unit factors. This proves the induction base.

The coherent foundation is Van der Put, *Rigid analytic spaces*, GAU 3 (1975--76), no.2, expose J7, 2.14--2.16.3: for a Tate algebra A, a finite A-module N gives the coherent sheaf U->O(U) tensor_A N; coherence can be checked on an affinoid G-cover; H^0 is N and H^i=0 for i>0. Its entire immediate argument is descent along A->B=product O(U_i), with B completed-tensor_A B=product O(U_i intersect U_j). Finite B-modules with compatible descent data descend, and the associated Hom equalizer is exact. The printed page abbreviates the descent condition; it must include its cocycle. Our transition map and its inverse satisfy it. The page explicitly cites Kiehl for the deeper descent theorem. The actual PDF one-based page 10, printed J7-09, was visually read in this turn; this is distinct from any historic native pixel claim.

Induct on the number k of wide factors. Let Z=A(r,R) times Y, 0<r<R in |K*|, with k wide factors. Both C(r) times Y and D(R) times Y have k-1. For an arbitrary line bundle L on Z, trivialize L on C(r) times Y. Glue it to the trivial line bundle on D(r) times Y using this frame. Indeed D(r) times Y and A(r,R) times Y are rational domains covering D(R) times Y and meet exactly in C(r) times Y. If |a|=r, the inequalities are |z/a|<=1 and |a/z|<=1. The denominator a is a unit, and (a,z) is the unit ideal, so both domains are legitimate rational localizations. Products with Y preserve this cover. Coherent G-descent produces an invertible sheaf on D(R) times Y. It is trivial by induction, hence L is trivial. This is sheaf descent on a finite G-cover, not an ordinary-open psh argument. It proves every finite product and every P_m over the retained K. Neither pro-Picard invariance nor topological contractibility is used.

## The genuine nonalgebraizable base-field surface

Put T=(G_m^2)^an, lambda_1=(t,2), lambda_2=(3,t), Lambda=<lambda_1,lambda_2>, X=T/Lambda. In x=(-log|z_1|,-log|z_2|), lambda(n) translates x by n in Z^2. Rectangles of widths less than one have disjoint nontrivial translates; their ordinary inverse images are quotient charts with deck transformations as transitions. The relation is a locally finite union of closed graphs: compact tropical ranges bound the possible integer differences. Hence the relation is a closed immersion into T times_K T.

The applied quotient foundations are Conrad--Temkin, *Non-archimedean analytification of algebraic spaces*, author version 24 February 2009, Lemmas 4.2.3--4.2.4 and the adjacent closed-immersion proof. Lemma 4.2.3 glues quotients of restrictions to an ordinary open cover, with open maps covering the resulting quotient; goodness and strictness follow if true on these charts. Its proof constructs the open overlap images from the two projections of the equivalence relation, descends their involution, checks triple overlaps, and glues. Lemma 4.2.4 gives coherent G-sheaf descent along any flat quasi-finite surjection of k-analytic spaces. Its immediate proof reduces locally to finite faithfully flat affinoid algebras, where completed tensors are ordinary tensors and algebraic descent applies. Closed immersions correspond to coherent ideals; descent of their ideals proves that a closed relation yields a closed quotient diagonal. These complete immediate applied arguments were read. The deeper Berkovich/descent foundations they cite remain named published inputs.

The strict compact polyannulus x^-1([0,1]^2) surjects onto X. To get a strict affinoid neighborhood about any lift, choose a center in (1/8 Z)^2 within 1/16 of its tropical point and take a closed rectangle of width 1/2 inside an open chart of width 3/4. Local torus charts give smoothness, pure dimension two and empty relative boundary. Compactness, separatedness and empty boundary imply analytic properness. Integral Laurent affinoids form a nested connected exhaustion of T, so X is connected. Thus X is good, strict, smooth, separated, proper and boundaryless over exactly K.

We next prove Pic(T)=0, including compatibility. For a unit f=sum b_beta z^beta on P_m put a=1/8. Its Gauss log norm, on log radii y in [-ma,ma]^2, is max_beta(log|b_beta|+beta dot y). This and the log norm of f^-1 are convex and sum to zero, hence affine. A term achieving the maximum at an interior point has the same affine function: the nonnegative affine difference vanishes inside a neighborhood and therefore has zero slope. If its exponent is alpha, vertex inequalities give |b_beta/b_alpha| exp(ma|beta-alpha|_1)<=1. Consequently f=b_alpha z^alpha(1+g), with zero constant coefficient in g and ||g||_(P_j)<=|s|^(m-j) for j<m. The first factor remains a unit on P_m; no strict smallness on its boundary is asserted. On all R^2 a distinct exponent would dominate on a ray, so a global unit of T is exactly a scalar monomial.

For a line bundle choose frames e_m on P_m by the finite theorem. Normalize successive frames by scalar monomials so e_(m+1)|P_m=(1+g_m)e_m. For each fixed j, p_j=product_(m=j)^infinity(1+g_m)|P_j converges to a unit: its first factor is a unit, later errors have norm at most |s|^(m-j), and inverse tails converge too. Then E_j=e_j p_j satisfies E_(j+1)|P_j=E_j. The P_j lie in the interiors of P_(j+1), so the admissible exhaustion glues these frames. This proves Pic(T)=0.

A pulled-back section of a line bundle on X is an analytic Laurent function f with f(lambda z)=c_lambda z^(h_lambda) f(z). Multipliers are global units. Commuting the generators gives lambda_1^(h_2)=lambda_2^(h_1). For h_1=(A,B), h_2=(C,D), this is t^C2^D=3^At^B. Valuations imply C=B, and prime factorization in Q* implies A=D=0. Thus h_1=(0,k), h_2=(k,0). If k!=0, choose n=(1,sign k), lambda=lambda(n), h=(kn_2,kn_1). Then Q=v(lambda^h)=2|k|>0. For any nonzero coefficient a_m the recurrence is a_(m+jh)=a_m c^j lambda^(-jm-hj(j+1)/2), j>=0. Its valuation has leading term -Qj(j+1)/2 and tends to minus infinity. This contradicts Laurent coefficient decay on the unit polyannulus. For k=0 any two nonzero exponents differ by a vector whose pairings with both period valuations vanish, hence they coincide. Nonzero sections are nowhere-zero monomials.

Every meromorphic function is covered by the following pole argument. On a local fraction chart F=g/h the intrinsic ideal J={b:bF is analytic} is the kernel of multiplication by g into O/(h), hence coherent. Smooth affinoid algebras are regular and noetherian. Stacks 0AG0 says every regular local ring is a UFD; its immediate proof inducts on dimension, localizes away from a prime regular parameter and uses Pic(R_f)=0 to make each height-one prime principal. Stacks 031T says for a noetherian normal domain R, R=intersection_(height p=1) R_p inside Frac(R). Its immediate proof uses S2, absence of embedded primes in R/aR, and tests membership in aR at its height-one associated primes. Both entire immediate proofs were read. Local UFD cancellation makes J finite locally free of rank one. Flat analytic restriction and coherent descent glue these intrinsic ideals, including every pole divisor. No global fraction equalizer theorem is substituted for the analytic meromorphic sheaf.

Trivialize J on T. Its inclusion into O gives f_0; by the defining property of J, f_1=Ff_0 is analytic. Invariance of F identifies the translates of J with J, so the two analytic functions have the same scalar-monomial multipliers. The preceding recurrence forces both to be multiples of the same monomial. Hence Gamma(X,M)=K.

If a separated finite-type K-algebraic space Y had Y^an=X, Conrad--Temkin 2.3.1 reflects smoothness and Example 2.3.2 compares closed-point residue fields and completed local rings. The theorem's exact other properties are separated, monomorphism, surjective, isomorphism, open immersion, flat, smooth, etale; for a finite-type morphism also closed immersion, finite, proper and quasi-finite. Its immediate proof reduces etale-locally to schemes, uses Chow's lemma for properness and scheme comparison for isomorphisms; smoothness follows through the same descent and local-ring comparisons. Thus Y is smooth of dimension two and connected. Regular components of a noetherian space are disjoint and open, so Y is integral.

The exact generic-field hypotheses are not suppressed. Stacks 0BB1 gives equivalence of finite-component conditions on quasi-compact etale charts; noetherian finite-type charts satisfy them. There are no embedded weak associates on regular charts. Separatedness implies decency and field monomorphisms at generic points. Stacks 086U gives a dense open scheme locus for a decent space; the unique generic point of integral Y lies there. Stacks 0ENA, under these three hypotheses, identifies the meromorphic sheaf with the locally finite sum/product of generic local-ring sheaves and Gamma with rational functions. Stacks 0EN6 gives total fractions on affine etale charts under its first two hypotheses. Stacks 0END identifies rational functions of an integral algebraic space with its generic field. Their complete statements and immediate proofs were read: reduce to affine etale charts, where the total fraction ring is the product of minimal-prime localizations; etale base change preserves this, and the dense scheme locus identifies the rational field. A dense affine scheme open and Noether normalization give trdeg_K K(Y)=2.

Analytic injection requires a separate argument. On regular Y a rational function has a Cartier pole ideal and numerator/denominator sections of the associated line bundle, descending through etale charts. Conrad--Temkin end of 2.3 and 3.3 constructs an exact coherent analytification functor by etale descent, independent of chart and compatible with pullback. Ducros, *Families of Berkovich spaces*, 2.1.4 states: for a scheme locally of finite type over an affinoid algebra, every algebraic-to-analytic local-ring map is regular. It cites Berkovich 1993, Proposition 2.6.2 for flatness and Ducros 2009, Theorem 3.3 for regularity; those are deeper foundations, not proofs contained in this memoir. Here the base K is affinoid. The local flat map is faithfully flat and preserves nonzerodivisors, so the ratio of the descended analytified sections is analytic meromorphic. A closed point of a dense affine scheme open avoiding numerator and denominator zeros detects every nonzero rational function analytically; its finite residue extension of K is complete. Thus K(Y) embeds over K into Gamma(X,M)=K, contradicting transcendence degree two. This excludes every separated finite-type K-algebraic space, with no claim after arbitrary extension of K.

## Ordinary bounded class, operator and normalization

On a deck sheet let x_j=-log|z_j|, q=|x|^2/2, DD=d'd'', theta=DDq. The deck change q(x+n)-q(x)=n dot x+|n|^2/2 is smooth DD-null; theta descends without an algebraic polarization. Define C_theta as continuous real u such that q+u is locally on ordinary opens a locally uniform limit of ordinary CLD smooth functions with middle-positive Hessian. No recognition of all classical or larger generated psh is asserted.

The applied CLD source is arXiv:1204.6277v2, submitted 25 July 2025, internal title 29 July 2025, 608 pages. Its 15.7.1--2 applies to a topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space with its analytic boundary and gives the canonical calibrated tropical level n, compatible with domains. Here n=2 and the boundary is empty. Its ordinary moment charts 15.1.1--2 and local-separation/cutoff/density statements 15.2.2--9 apply because X is good, separated and compact. In particular compact symmetric tests can be decomposed inside their prescribed ordinary open into two compact middle-positive tests (6.5.2). Immediate proofs use ordinary unit moments and smooth partitions about the compact support; deeper calibration/analytic foundations remain published inputs.

Here is the needed order-zero argument independently. In a moment presentation the symmetric (p,p) coefficients are symmetric matrices on Lambda^p R^m. The middle cone is PSD; if lambda is the Euclidean positive (1,1) form, lambda^p is p! times the identity. It bounds any smooth symmetric matrix on a compact tropical support above and below. Multiply by a cutoff and localize by a finite partition to get beta=eta_+-eta_- with compact positive tests in the same open. For a symmetric middle-positive current T, phi-><T,phi eta> is a positive scalar functional, bounded on compact sets by a plateau cutoff times ||phi||. Smooth scalar density and Riesz give coefficient Radon measures. Subtracting the two measures for beta is independent of decomposition by equality on smooth tests; continuous multiplication is defined and |<bT,beta>|<=sup_K|b|<T,eta_++eta_->. If T_j->T positively and b_j->b locally uniformly, approximate b by smooth g and split b_jT_j-bT=(b_j-g)T_j+g(T_j-T)+(g-b)T. The first and last terms tend uniformly to zero with the approximation error and the middle tends weakly to zero. This proves the multiplication continuity needed below.

The strong cone cannot replace this argument: for m=4,p=2, Sym(Lambda^2 R^4) has dimension 21. Strong squares satisfy Q=w12w34-w13w24+w14w23=0 and span exactly 20 dimensions. Write Q=x dot y. A quadratic vanishing on Q=0 has no pure x/y part and has mixed matrix B with B^t x proportional to every x; basis vectors and their sums force B scalar. Thus its annihilator is exactly Q. The nondecomposable witness e12+e34 has Q=1. The printed strong domination in CLD 7.2.9 is not an applied premise.

For a closed symmetric T and smooth h, complementary-degree Leibniz and symmetry give DD(hT)=DDh wedge T. Arbitrary continuous multiplication is not claimed to preserve closedness, and the overbroad CLD 8.6.7 is not used. For u,v in C_theta, f=q+u, g=q+v, define B(u,v)=DD(f DD[g]) locally. Smooth-positive approximants and the preceding multiplication lemma show this is the weak limit of the smooth mixed products. Thus it is positive, symmetric, independent of approximants, local and uniformly continuous in the bounded class. Smooth DD-null changes glue it. Difference multilinearity follows by subtraction. This is the bounded argument underlying CLD 8.5.1, 8.5.3, 8.7.1--4 and 8.8.4--8; their full immediate arguments were checked and no unbounded continuity is extracted from them.

CLD 14.3.1--5 constructs canonical calibration using the actual finite flat local degree after a torus projection; 14.5.2--3 describes the image calibration with the sum of these degrees. Its invariance proof compares torus projections by finite isogenies and their determinants, and restricts through common refined cells. Generic Artinian lengths are part of this degree, not discarded. CLD 5.8.1--6 realizes calibrated top forms as analytic measures on the moment skeleton. For the identity and translated identity moments used here the map is an actual analytic isomorphism, with degree one and saturated lattice Z^2. Consequently theta^2=2 i_*dx, where dx is probability Haar measure on R^2/Z^2. The factor 2 is the exterior 2!, and raw mass is two.

Globally B(u,v)=theta wedge alpha_v+DD(u alpha_v), alpha_u=theta+DD[u], and theta wedge alpha_v=theta^2+DD(v theta). Pairing the differentiated currents with 1 on compact boundaryless X gives zero. Therefore B always has mass two and MA_theta(u)=B(u,u) is a genuine positive analytic Radon measure. Dini gives decreasing continuity only when the limit is still continuous in C_theta. Convex nondecreasing regularizations of max show convexity and finite-max stability. For w=max(u,v-epsilon), locality and equal mass give MA(v){u<v-epsilon}<=MA(u){u<=v-epsilon}. Both sets increase to {u<v} as epsilon decreases to zero, proving bounded comparison. This proves neither full-domain comparison nor uniqueness.

## Whole branch and circle chain

On R/Z let G(y)=y^2/2-y/2+1/12 on [0,1], periodically extended. It has mean zero, G''=dy-delta_0, range [-1/24,1/12] and Lipschitz constant 1/2. Put u0=-G(x_1)-G(x_2), A=alpha_u0. Periodic positive convolution and bounded continuity give A^2=2delta_i(0) and theta wedge A=i_*(dy tensor delta_0+delta_0 tensor dy). The entire fibre F=tau^-1(0) has u0=-1/6.

On the ordinary sheet |x_j|<1/4 define, for N>=1, ell_j=log max(exp(-N),|z_j-1|), b_j=log max(1,|z_j|), d_j=ell_j-b_j, D_N=max(d_1,d_2), U_N=u0+D_N. Each d_j<=0 and vanishes when |z_j|!=1. Thus D_N vanishes off F and extends by zero. Its negative locus is the ordinary open W={|z_1-1|<1,|z_2-1|<1}. Directly, q+U_N=max(ell_1+b_2,b_1+ell_2)-(1/2)log|z_1z_2|-1/6. Near a zero of z_j-1, ell_j is constant and the inactive logarithmic coordinate is omitted. Elsewhere the units give ordinary moment charts and convex softmax gives smooth-positive approximants. Hence U_N lies in exactly C_theta.

On W put w_j=z_j-1. The local weight is log max(exp(-N),|w_1|,|w_2|)-1/6. At the translated Gauss point xi_N with w-radii exp(-N), a softmax of max(0,y_1,y_2), y_j=log|w_j|+N, has gradient mapping R^2 diffeomorphically onto the open triangle p_j>0, p_1+p_2<1. Its Hessian determinant integral is 1/2; rescaling concentrates at zero. The exterior factor 2 and actual degree-one Gauss section give MA(U_N)|W=delta_xi_N. Away from the vertex the weight, after an affine subtraction, uses one coordinate; at zeros omit inactive logs. Its square is zero. The previous companion correctly leaves the other mass one unidentified; n2 below identifies it by a new argument.

Since theta=A=0 on W and D_N=0 on its complement including the boundary, coefficient measures give D_N theta=D_N A=0. Thus theta wedge alpha_U_N=theta wedge A and MA(U_N) is supported on F. Define E(u)=(1/3)integral u(theta^2+theta wedge alpha_u+MA(u)). The three integrals for U_N are 0, -1/6, -1/3-N, so E(U_N)=-1/6-N/3. For V_(a,N)=u0+aD_N, 0<=a<=1, A wedge DD D_N=DD(D_N A)=0; expansion gives MA(V)=(1-a^2)MA(u0)+a^2MA(U_N) and E(V)=-1/6-a^3N/3. Its supremum is 1/12 and its rigid value at y=(1,1) is -1/6-aN. Setting a=N^(-1/3) and subtracting the supremum gives sup v_N=0, E(v_N)=-2/3 and v_N(y)=-1/4-N^(2/3). Only uniform relative compactness fails. Skeleton reference L1 is not separated, since all these restrictions coincide.

For a raw-mass-two mu with bounded dual M=sup_C_theta(E(u)-integral u dmu)<infinity, put J0=E(u0)-integral u0 dmu, C=M-J0. Testing V gives aL_N-a^3N/3<=C, L_N=integral(-D_N)dmu. For N>3C/2 the a=1 test forces L_N<=N; optimizing at sqrt(L_N/N) gives L_N<=(3C/2)^(2/3)N^(1/3). Since -D_N=N on B_N={|w_j|<=exp(-N)}, mu(B_N)<=(3C/2)^(2/3)N^(-2/3). This is necessary only. The rigid atom 2delta_y has infinite bounded dual and is ineligible as an original counterexample.

The entire circle chain can be proved without an imported equation theorem. If H={continuous h:rho_h=dy+h''>=0}, then rho_h has mass one and h=-G*rho_h+c. The mean-zero family has range [-1/12,1/24], Lipschitz constant 1/2 and oscillation <=1/8, so sup-zero normalization is uniformly compact by Arzela--Ascoli. For S_theta={h_1(tau_1)+h_2(tau_2):h_j in H}, convolution gives B(h_1+h_2,k_1+k_2)=i_*(rho_h1 tensor rho_k2+rho_k1 tensor rho_h2) and MA(h_1+h_2)=2i_*(rho_h1 tensor rho_h2). Hence every such skeletal product measure has a solution unique modulo constants within S_theta.

Put e(h)=integral h dy-(1/2)integral|h'|^2dy. Convolution converges uniformly and in derivative L2 and proves integral h d rho_h=integral h dy-integral|h'|^2 and e(k)-e(h)=integral(k-h)d rho_h-(1/2)integral|k'-h'|^2. Thus E_sep(h_1+h_2)=2(e(h_1)+e(h_2)) is the three-term bounded energy. For any analytic mass-two mu its restricted objective sees only nu_j=(tau_j)_*mu/2 and is maximized by rho_hj=nu_j. Its resulting MA is their skeletal product; it need not equal mu. Sup-zero normalization gives 0<=E*_sep(mu)<=1/2; for the rigid atom the exact value is 1/6, contrasting with its infinite bounded dual.

For any continuous circle obstacle a, the largest H-minorant P(a) exists: constants give a lower bound; the common Lipschitz bound gives a finite continuous supremum; y^2/2+P(a) is a supremum of convex functions. Monotonicity and constant translation give sup-norm nonexpansiveness. If curvature charges a noncontact arc, replace the convex lift on a sufficiently short interior interval by its endpoint chord. The slope lies between the exterior slopes, and the increase is small enough to remain below the obstacle. Repeat on integer translates with the affine quasiperiodic correction. This contradicts maximality, so rho_P is supported on contact and integral(a-P)d rho_P=0. For p_b=P(a+bv), energy differences and the two contact statements yield b integral v d rho_pb<=e(p_b)-e(p)<=b integral v d rho_p. Uniform convergence and weak curvature convergence give derivative integral v d rho_p. This is all circle directions, not all analytic obstacles.

This finishes the independent reconstruction of every mathematical chain asserted in whole383. Its negative scope statements are correct: no full intrinsic unbounded domain, full-mass operator, separated weak compactness, all-obstacle envelope theorem, full first variation, sufficient measure criterion, every-admissible-measure existence or full uniqueness is established. The finite Picard/nonalgebraization foundation is a valid base-K foundation under the stated analytic inputs; it does not itself supply those missing assertions.

The full new standalone proof is assembled from notes/n1.md--n5.md in P16.7-independent-paper.tex and proof-companion.md. Full primary bodies and bound input copies are confined to sources-LOCALONLY and inputs-LOCALONLY. Rerun `python audit_and_build.py`; it executes only our standard-library diagnostics and document assembly, never supplied programs or a compiler. Detailed identities, source-reading limits and original residual are recorded in source-application-ledger.md and evidence/verdicts.json. Support: none.

notes.detailedSummary: For all positive real depths, MA(U_N)=delta_o+delta_xi_N. Refined unit moments identify the old unspecified mass at o. For coefficients c_i summing to C<=1, branch atom masses are successive differences of squared tails and the remaining mass is 2-C^2 at o. Square-root tail inversion solves every such finite target, with uniqueness within the finite family and exact energy. No full-class branch cap or full dual admissibility is inferred.

# Identifying the second atom and solving finite nested branch measures

Use the base-field X, real theta, exact ordinary bounded class C_theta and genuine bounded products reconstructed in n1. The following is a new scoped bounded theorem, not an unbounded finite-energy equation theorem. For every N>0,

MA_theta(U_N)=delta_i(0)+delta_xi_N.

The original construction works also for 0<N<1. Its proof uses only r=exp(-N)<1: d_j<=0 and d_j=0 when |z_j|!=1, the support is inside the same fibre/sheet, logarithmic zero coordinates are omitted, and ordinary convex softmax provides the same approximants. No rational-radius or strictness claim is added.

We first identify the previously unspecified mass. The measure is supported on F and has restriction delta_xi_N on W by n1. On F, |z_j|=1 implies |w_j|<=1. If |w_1|<1 and |w_2|=1, choose an ordinary neighborhood on which ell_1<ell_2+b_1-b_2, b_1=0 and ell_2=log|w_2|. Then q+U_N=log|w_2|-(1/2)log|z_1z_2|-1/6 is affine in logarithms of units and has zero Hessian. The other case is symmetric. This includes w_j=0 by omission of its inactive logarithm.

The remaining locus has |z_1|=|z_2|=|w_1|=|w_2|=1. On an ordinary neighborhood all four functions are units and the truncations are inactive. Here q+U_N is a convex maximum of the four affine forms log|w_1|, log|w_1|+log|z_2|, log|w_2|, log|w_2|+log|z_1|, minus a smooth affine form and a constant. The applied support statement is CLD-v2 8.8.6, with its entire immediate proof: a bounded tropical difference-of-convex product in a common moment chart is supported on that moment's top-dimensional skeleton. Smooth convex approximants have this support by 5.8.4; local uniform product continuity preserves support, and subtraction gives the difference-of-convex case. The moment here is f=(z_1,w_1,z_2,w_2).

To check its skeleton, CLD-v2 12.2.7--10 states that tropical dimension at a point is at most the graded residual transcendence degree of the subfield generated by the moment coordinates. In the boundaryless case equality holds. The complete immediate argument in 12.2.8 cites the published local tropical dimension theorem [50, Theorem 3.4]; that deeper analytic input remains explicitly cited, not newly proved. We use only the upper bound. At the displayed unit-norm locus, graded reductions satisfy w_j=z_j-1 and all coordinates have degree one. If the two reductions z_1,z_2 are dependent over the residue field C, the generated graded field has transcendence degree at most one over graded K, so the point is outside the top skeleton and the measure vanishes near it. If they are independent, for every Laurent polynomial sum a_beta z^beta, divide by a coefficient of maximal norm. Its nonzero reduction cannot vanish, so its norm equals max|a_beta|. This characterizes exactly the original unit Gauss point i(0), as also checked directly in CLD 12.1.5. Thus the complement of W contributes only at i(0). Total mass two and branch mass one prove the asserted identity. This is an actual analytic support argument, not a polyhedral inverse convention.

There is a larger finite equation family. Choose 0<N_1<...<N_k, c_i>=0 and C=sum c_i<=1, and put u_c=u0+sum c_i D_(N_i). Convexity of C_theta gives membership. Set b_i=sum_(j>i)c_j and p_i=(b_i+c_i)^2-b_i^2. Then

MA_theta(u_c)=(2-C^2)delta_i(0)+sum p_i delta_xi_(N_i).

Proof: on W, the local weight, up to an affine term and constant, is sum c_i max(-N_i,log|w_1|,log|w_2|). Between successive depths it is affine plus a multiple of max(log|w_1|,log|w_2|), whose square vanishes. At xi_(N_i), set y_j=log|w_j|+N_i. The shallower truncations are locally constant and the deeper ones are locally untruncated. The remaining weight is

b_i max(y_1,y_2)+c_i max(0,y_1,y_2)
=max(b_i y_1,b_i y_2,(b_i+c_i)y_1,(b_i+c_i)y_2).

Its gradient polygon has vertices b_i e_1,b_i e_2,(b_i+c_i)e_1,(b_i+c_i)e_2 and area ((b_i+c_i)^2-b_i^2)/2. For c_i>0 its softmax gradient is a diffeomorphism onto the polygon interior: the Hessian is the positive covariance of the slope vectors, hence positive definite; strict convexity gives injectivity, and minimizing the softmax minus any interior linear functional gives surjectivity. Change of variables gives the determinant integral equal to polygon area, and rescaling concentrates at zero. For c_i=0 the polygon has no area and the square is zero. Actual degree-one translated Gauss sections and the exterior 2 give the claimed mass p_i. Points with a zero coordinate are handled by omission. Thus the only branch atoms are these xi_(N_i), and their total mass telescopes to C^2.

Outside W but on F, if exactly one |w_j|<1, the U_(N_i) weights are affine there while the u0 weight depends, apart from an affine term, on the other z coordinate alone; hence the top product vanishes. At all four unit norms the same common moment support argument just proved applies to their convex combination. The remaining mass 2-C^2 is therefore at i(0). This proves the formula for genuine bounded products on X.

Consequently every measure

mu=(2-P)delta_i(0)+sum p_i delta_xi_(N_i), p_i>=0, P=sum p_i<=1,

has an explicit bounded solution. Put T_i=sum_(j>=i)p_j, T_(k+1)=0, c_i=sqrt(T_i)-sqrt(T_(i+1)). Then b_i=sqrt(T_(i+1)), C=sqrt(P)<=1 and the preceding formula gives exactly mu. The coefficients are recovered from its branch masses, so uniqueness modulo constants holds within this fixed finite branch family. No uniqueness across C_theta or an unconstructed E1 class follows. This includes off-original-skeleton analytic support. It is a genuinely computed Monge--Ampere equation, not a surrogate measure assignment.

For every such u_c the three energy integrals are 0, -1/6, and -1/3-S, where

S=sum_i p_i sum_j c_j min(N_i,N_j).

Indeed D_(N_j) theta=D_(N_j) A=0, all MA support is in F, u0=-1/6 there, D_(N_j)(i(0))=0 and D_(N_j)(xi_(N_i))=-min(N_i,N_j). Thus E(u_c)=-1/6-S/3. This is finite bounded energy with the fixed raw mass two. It does not prove finite dual energy over all C_theta, and it is not offered as a definition of full admissibility. The coefficient restriction C<=1 gives a branch mass <=1 only for THIS family. No universal mass cap is asserted.

The complete new theorem and proof are in this note and P16.7-independent-paper.tex. The moment source units, full CLD body and exact source-reading intervals are retained locally. Rerun `python audit_and_build.py` for rational diagnostic rows and document identity checks; these are finite observations, not the analytic proof. Support: n1.

# Exact branch-family dual at the actual finite-depth Dirac point

Use n1's bounded calculus and n2's finite branch family. Let B be all u_c=u0+sum c_i D_(N_i)+constant with finitely many depths N_i>0, c_i>=0, sum c_i<=1, including the empty sum. Constants do not affect a raw-mass-two dual. B is a concrete subset of C_theta. Fix any finite N0>0 and the ACTUAL analytic point xi_(N0) in W; this is distinct from the rigid point (1,1).

The exact result is

sup_(u in B)(E(u)-2u(xi_(N0)))=1/6+5N0/3,

attained by U_(N0). This proves only a restricted dual value, not finite dual energy over C_theta or over a full intrinsic E1 class.

Here is an all-parameters proof, not finite numerical evidence. For a finite sum define its decreasing tail C(t)=sum_(N_i>=t)c_i for t>0. It takes values in [0,1] and vanishes beyond the largest depth. At xi_(N0), sum c_i(-D_(N_i))=sum c_i min(N0,N_i)=integral_0^N0 C(t)dt. The branch mass tail at depth t is sum_(N_i>=t)p_i=C(t)^2 by the telescoping formula in n2. Tonelli on finite nonnegative sums gives

S=sum_i p_i sum_j c_j min(N_i,N_j)=integral_0^infinity C(t)^3dt.

Thus the objective is

1/6+integral_0^N0 (2C(t)-C(t)^3/3)dt
      -(1/3)integral_N0^infinity C(t)^3dt.

On [0,1], 2c-c^3/3 is increasing and its maximum is 5/3. The tail term is nonpositive. Hence the objective is at most 1/6+5N0/3. Take C(t)=1 on (0,N0) and zero after N0, namely U_(N0), to obtain equality. For the older single-pencil tests this same formula reduces to E(V_(a,N))-2V_(a,N)(xi_(N0))=1/6+2a min(N,N0)-a^3N/3; there is no divergence as N tends to infinity at fixed xi_(N0).

More generally for mu_p=(2-p)delta_i(0)+p delta_xi_(N0), 0<=p<=2, the B-dual is

1/6+N0 times [ (2/3)p^(3/2) if 0<=p<=1;
                      p-1/3 if 1<=p<=2 ].

Replace 2C by pC in the preceding objective. The maximizing value on [0,1] of pc-c^3/3 occurs at c=sqrt(p) when p<=1 and at c=1 when p>=1; the tail is again best zero. This proves the exact formula and attainment by V_(sqrt(p),N0) or U_(N0), respectively. For p<=1 the maximizing potential's actual MA is mu_p by n2. For p>1 its actual MA is delta_i(0)+delta_xi_(N0), which differs from mu_p. In particular the B-maximizer for 2delta_xi_(N0) is NOT a solution. This explicit calculation exhibits the difference between restricted variational optimization and solving the genuine equation.

The only implication for the full bounded dual is the lower bound E*_C_theta(2delta_xi_(N0))>=1/6+5N0/3. It provides no upper bound. No universal analytic atom cap or local Newton-body bound for arbitrary all-direction psh potentials is proved. In particular, the inability of B to realize branch mass two cannot show nonexistence in C_theta or in any full-mass E1 extension. The infinite-dual rigid test cannot be transplanted to this finite-depth point. Both full-dual admissibility and a full-domain solution/universal obstruction remain unresolved.

Artifacts: notes/n3.md, proof-companion.md, P16.7-independent-paper.tex and evidence/diagnostics.json. Rerun `python audit_and_build.py`; its exact finite rational rows merely check algebraic instances of the universal tail argument above. Support: n1, n2.

notes.text:
# A restricted intrinsic unbounded radial energy theory

Use the analytic X, theta and bounded calculus of n1 and the genuine finite-branch products of n2. This is a complete new scoped construction on the actual analytic space, with a deliberately restricted radial domain. It is not the full all-direction psh/E1 class, and its measure range is not the original admissibility criterion. Fix a discrete sequence 0<N_1<N_2<... tending to infinity. Let y=(1,1), o=i(0). All radii are real analytic Gauss radii; no strictness assertion at these radii is required.

Define the continuous extended depth R:X->[0,infinity] by R=-log max(|w_1|,|w_2|) on W and R=0 on its complement. At the boundary of W the maximum norm tends to one; near the boundary of the sheet W is absent. Its only infinite value is at y. Every D_N=-min(N,R). For c_i>=0 with C=sum c_i<=1, define

T(t)=sum_(N_i>=t)c_i, H(r)=integral_0^r T(t)dt,
u=u0-H(R)+b, b in R,

with the canonical limiting value at y, possibly minus infinity. Denote this domain by Gamma. H is increasing, concave, 1-Lipschitz on finite intervals, H(0)=0, and T decreases to zero. The partial sums u_m=u0+sum_(i<=m)c_iD_(N_i)+b decrease to u. On each compact subset of X\{y}, R is bounded, and the omitted terms are bounded by sup R times sum_(i>m)c_i. Thus convergence is locally uniform there. The common moment presentations from n1--n2, with inactive zero coordinates omitted, show q+u is locally uniformly approximable by ordinary smooth-positive weights there. Hence the local bounded operator is already defined on X\{y}; no operator is assigned merely to an unsupported global limit.

Put C_i=sum_(j>=i)c_j. By n2 and local uniform continuity, the actual local top measure has atoms p_i=C_i^2-C_(i+1)^2 at xi_(N_i) and mass 2-C^2 at o. Away from those points at finite depth the same local moments give zero top measure. Since C_i->0, sum p_i=C^2. Extending the local measure by zero at y gives a positive analytic Radon measure of FULL raw mass two:

MA(u)=(2-C^2)delta_o+sum_i(C_i^2-C_(i+1)^2)delta_xi_(N_i).

This agrees with the bounded operator whenever u is bounded: H(infinity)<infinity is equivalent to sum c_i N_i<infinity, and then the partial sums converge uniformly on all X. If u is unbounded, H(infinity)=infinity and its singular locus is exactly {y}. The canonical nonpluripolar recipe is directly verified. The continuous theta-positive truncation u^(M)=u0+b-min(H(R),M) is locally max(u,u0+b-M). If H(infinity)<=M it is already the bounded u. Otherwise it is constant relative to u0 near y. It belongs to C_theta: in the latter case clipped finite sums converge locally uniformly off y in the common moment charts, are eventually exactly constant relative to u0 on a neighborhood of y, and convex max regularization gives ordinary approximants. On {H(R)<M}, bounded locality gives exactly the constructed local product. The extra clamp atom is excluded by this strict set. As M increases the restricted products exhaust the local measure off y; omitted branch tail tends to zero because it is bounded by T(r)^2 at depth r and T(r)->0. Their mass therefore tends to two. The operator is obtained from genuine bounded local products by the full-mass nonpluripolar truncation recipe, not an inverse measure declaration. Ordinary truncations max(u,-j) yield the same recipe: for all sufficiently large j, only W is truncated, where u0=-1/6, and these are exactly the same clamps with M=j+b-1/6.

Mixed products are constructed locally as well. For u,v with tails T,S on this fixed grid, their local bounded mixed product on X\{y}, extended by zero at y, is

B(u,v)=(2-C_u C_v)delta_o
        +sum_i(C_i^u C_i^v-C_(i+1)^u C_(i+1)^v)delta_xi_(N_i).

Polarize n2's finite formula using genuine bounded products and then pass locally uniformly off y. The displayed branch masses are nonnegative because both tails decrease. They sum to C_u C_v; both tails tend to zero. Thus this mixed product is positive, symmetric, local and has mass two. Truncating each potential checks mixed full mass by the same tail argument. The theta-mixed measure remains theta wedge A and theta^2 retains its raw mass-two normalization. No full-class unbounded wedge theorem is invoked.

For b=0 the three energy integrals are 0, -1/6, and -1/3-integral_0^infinity T(t)^3dt. The first two measures are supported away from the singular point, and D_N annihilates theta and A. For the top measure Tonelli gives

sum_i p_i H(N_i)
=integral_0^infinity T(t) [sum_(N_i>=t)p_i]dt
=integral_0^infinity T(t)^3dt.

Negative parts are handled by this nonnegative identity; there is no infinity cancellation. Define Gamma^1 by finiteness of this tail integral. This is exactly finiteness of the genuine three-term energy in Gamma, and

E(u)=-1/6-(1/3)integral T^3+2b.

Canonical finite sums have tails increasing to T, so monotone convergence proves their energies converge to E(u); their actual MA measures converge weakly with all tail mass accounted for. A concrete unbounded example is N_i=i and c_i=1/(i(i+1)). Then C_i=1/i, C=1, H(infinity)=sum_i1/(i+1)=infinity, whereas integral T^3=sum_i1/i^3<infinity by the integral test. Thus u(y)=-infinity and u has finite energy in this intrinsic domain. Its MA is delta_o+sum_i(1/i^2-1/(i+1)^2)delta_xi_i, of mass two and with no rigid atom. No exact zeta value is needed.

Every segment first variation inside Gamma^1 holds. On a segment with tails T_t=(1-t)T+tS, differentiation is justified by (T+S)^3<=4(T^3+S^3) and Holder. The derivative is -integral(S-T)T_t^2, plus twice the derivative of b. The potential difference on X\{y} is -integral_0^R(S-T), plus the constant difference. Signed Fubini is justified by Holder in L3 and L(3/2), and integration against MA(u_t) gives exactly the derivative. The measure has no atom at y, so no undefined difference of two minus infinities is integrated. Hence dE(u_t)/dt=integral(v-u)MA(u_t) for every direction within Gamma^1. The second derivative is -2integral(S-T)^2T_t<=0. Thus E is concave. If v<=u pointwise off y, segment variation is nonpositive and E(v)<=E(u). These are domain-specific variational statements.

Comparison also holds within Gamma. Take canonical finite sums u_m,v_m on the same fixed grid. Their measures converge in total variation: each fixed atomic mass converges, the mass at o converges, and the branch tail after depth N_k is uniformly at most (C_(k+1))^2. Their potentials converge locally uniformly off y. Choose epsilon>0 avoiding the countably many values v(x)-u(x) at x=o and x=xi_(N_i). In the bounded comparison inequality for u_m,v_m, strict-set indicators therefore stabilize at each fixed atom. The total-variation convergence and the uniform branch-tail bound pass the inequality to MA(v){u<v-epsilon}<=MA(u){u<=v-epsilon}. Both sides give zero mass to y. Let epsilon decrease to zero along noncritical values; monotone convergence gives MA(v){u<v}<=MA(u){u<v}. This does not compare a Gamma potential with an arbitrary outside-class potential.

There is a useful separated compactness theorem within Gamma^1. All b=0 potentials have supremum 1/12, since H>=0 and a maximum of u0 lies outside F; normalize by subtracting 1/12. Fix integral T^3<=L. Monotonicity gives r T(r)^3<=L. Thus the coefficient tail at depth r is at most (L/r)^(1/3), and the MA tail is at most (L/r)^(2/3). Diagonal extraction gives convergence of every c_i. The uniform coefficient-tail estimate prevents loss of their total sum and gives uniform convergence of H on each finite interval. The limit still has sum c_i<=1 and, by Fatou, integral T^3<=L. Potentials converge uniformly on every compact subset of X\{y}. This topology is separated on Gamma: H determines every jump coefficient and the canonical value at y, while normalization determines b. It is compact, not just sequentially compact: the coefficient parameter set is a closed subset of the compact metrizable product [0,1]^N; the uniform tail estimate gives the claimed topology continuously on that set. The actual MA measures converge weakly on X by convergence of each atomic coefficient and the uniform mass-tail estimate. This is a specified separated weak replacement within Gamma, not on all analytic potentials.

Decreasing continuity holds under the energy bound. If normalized u_m in Gamma^1 decrease pointwise with integral T_m^3<=L, their H_m increase to a finite continuous 1-Lipschitz concave H on each finite interval. Slopes on each fixed grid interval converge, determining the limit coefficients. Fatou and the tail estimate show T(infinity)=0 and integral T^3<=L, so the limit is in Gamma^1. Compactness then gives local uniform convergence off y and weak convergence of the actual MA measures. Energy converges too: first variation gives E(u_m)>=E(u), so integral T_m^3<=integral T^3; Fatou supplies the opposite liminf inequality. This is decreasing continuity in the declared energy-bounded radial domain, not for arbitrary analytic psh sequences.

The equation range is explicit. Given nonnegative p_i with P=sum p_i<=1 and no rigid atom, put P_i=sum_(j>=i)p_j, c_i=sqrt(P_i)-sqrt(P_(i+1)). Then C=sqrt(P)<=1 and the genuine operator constructed above equals (2-P)delta_o+sum p_i delta_xi_(N_i). It has finite energy in Gamma exactly when

integral_0^infinity P_tail(t)^(3/2)dt<infinity,
P_tail(t)=sum_(N_i>=t)p_i.

The operator recovers C_i=sqrt(P_i), hence every c_i. Thus uniqueness modulo constants holds in Gamma^1. This is a complete equation computation for this chosen range. P<=1 describes this constructed domain's range and is NOT declared full intrinsic admissibility.

For measures in that range the dual over the entire Gamma^1 domain can also be computed. For a test tail T, nonnegative Tonelli first yields the extended-valued expression E(u)-integral u dmu=1/6+integral(P_tail T-T^3/3). When P_tail^(3/2) is integrable, Holder justifies the finite signed expression. Pointwise Young optimization at T=sqrt(P_tail), a permitted decreasing grid tail, gives the dual 1/6+(2/3)integral P_tail^(3/2). If this integral is infinite, finite grid cutoffs of the optimizing coefficients give objectives tending to infinity, so the restricted dual is infinite. Indeed their tails increase to sqrt(P_tail), and for those tails the objective is nonnegative and increases to (2/3)P_tail^(3/2) pointwise; monotone convergence applies. This restricted criterion exactly matches energies of solutions in this range. For P>1 the upper slope constraint is active: n3 gives a finite restricted dual for 2delta_xi_(N0) when the grid contains N0, although no Gamma solution exists. Full original admissibility is therefore not settled by this criterion.

This supplies an intrinsic UNBOUNDED special class, genuine mixed/full-mass products, finite energy, comparison, separated compactness and its own variations/equations. It supplies neither arbitrary analytic support nor arbitrary all-direction psh potentials, and no all-obstacle envelope theorem is claimed. The original target remains open. The retained space is the good strict smooth connected separated proper boundaryless two-dimensional analytic quotient over K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), with periods (s^8,2),(3,s^8). Its real analytic theta datum has raw mass two and no ample algebraic line bundle. The finite Picard argument is correct at base K and suffices to prove nonalgebraization by every separated finite-type K-algebraic space. No arbitrary-extension statement is needed or granted.

The exact new scope is: all positive real depths; an actual two-atom identity MA(U_N)=delta_i(0)+delta_xi_N; explicit bounded solutions for every finite nested-branch atomic measure with total branch mass <=1 and remaining mass at i(0); its complete energy formula; and an exact finite restricted-dual value 1/6+5N0/3 for the actual finite-depth mass-two Dirac. What remains is an intrinsic all-direction unbounded psh/E1/full-mass domain for this real analytic positivity datum, a rigorous comparison with C_theta and identical bounded energy, genuine unbounded mixed/top products and decreasing continuity, useful normalized energy-bounded compactness in a specified separated weak topology, envelopes and orthogonality for every analytic obstacle, full energy first variation, the correct mass-two finite-energy measure criterion, existence for EVERY eligible measure with arbitrary analytic support, and uniqueness modulo constants in the FULL domain. A decreasing limit outside the continuous class cannot be assigned an operator just from the established uniform continuity.
